power.after: AC, 100%; no thermal or performance warning recorded

host.backgroundActivity: Independent Rider and Xprotect processes were consuming CPU before measurement. No applications were stopped, no CPU affinity was imposed, and load was not continuously sampled.

fingerprints.reproduction: Measured Neri executable is byte-identical to a rebuild with the published source, verified stage3 frontend, and the listed native components; output basename is kept identical for Mach-O signing.

method.order: Four cyclic configuration orders; alternating worker order. Every process and sample is retained.
method.timer: Monotonic milliseconds. Kernel includes scheduling, result allocation, join, checked reduction and collection. Process metrics also include warmup, setup, startup and reporting.
method.baseline: One-worker batch uses the ordinary sequential loop in both languages; larger worker counts use tasks.generate or Parallel.For.
method.statistic: Median of four process medians. Speedup T(1)/T(p), nominal efficiency T(1)/(p*T(p)). Different M4 core classes are not equal-capacity processors.
method.correctness: Every invocation checks its checksum against an independent mathematical oracle; all 128 processes exited zero.

limitations: One host and one session with other applications active; not a controlled claim of optimality or a universal language ranking.
A batch of 64 independent recurrence chains does not characterize allocation-heavy tasks, tiny-task overhead, bandwidth saturation or irregular dependency graphs.
Four independent processes are not enough for a strong confidence-bound claim; within-process samples are dependent.
This shared-queue executor is not Cilk's work-stealing scheduler; the Cilk optimality theorem is not claimed.
These ARM64 results do not establish native x86-64 scaling.
